section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the principle of "as water reflects a face back to a face, so the heart of man to man" in both interpersonal and Divine terms, emphasizing that the lower person's arousal from below generates a corresponding arousal from above.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing what is said,
"As water reflects a face back to a face, so the heart of man to man,"
and it is explained in Chassidus,
that "the heart of man to man" does not refer only to two human beings,
[meaning] that the heart of a man in his love for his fellow arouses his fellow's love for him,
but also [refers] to the lower man and the upper Man,
that according to the manner of the service of the lower man,
the arousal from below,
so is the manner of the arousal from above,
the drawing down from the upper Man to the lower man,
"as water reflects a face back to a face."
And it may be said,
that the comparison of "the heart of man to man" to "water reflects a face back to a face" is,
that just as in water [reflecting] a face back to a face,
that which appears to the man [as] the form that he shows in the water is because through his looking into the water, there are made
(appear)
in the water the form of the face looking into them, and this form is afterwards seen by the man looking,
so it is with "the heart of man to man,"
that that which through the service and arousal from below of the lower man, an arousal from above and a drawing down from the upper Man to the lower man is made,
it is,
because the service of the lower man ascends from below to above,
to the upper Man,
and through this there is made in Him
(a likeness of)
this matter,
and afterwards this matter is drawn down
(that was made in the upper Man)
from above to below,
to the lower man.
And to add,
in the analogy of water,
that the face of the man who looks into the water appears in the water,
it is only that it appears thus to the seeing eye,
and in the analogue,
through the service of the lower man there is made
(a likeness of)
this matter in the upper Man
(and not only that it appears thus).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that just as "the heart of man to man" applies spiritually, so too "as water reflects a face back to a face" refers to the upper waters of the simple Ein Sof, where the Sefiros are generated through the raising of feminine waters.
section.t: And behold, just as "the heart of man to man" is
(not only in its simple sense,
but)
also in spirituality
(in the upper Man and the lower man),
so too is it regarding the beginning of the verse "as water reflects a face back to a face,"
which speaks
(not only of water in its simple sense,
but)
also of the upper waters,
namely the simplicity of Ein Sof that is above the form of man.
And the matter of "as water reflects a face back to a face" is,
that although Ein Sof is absolutely simple and no form of Sefiros applies to Him,
nevertheless,
through the raising of feminine waters of the Sefiros to Ein Sof,
Sefiros are made in Him — the ten hidden Sefiros,
and the hidden Sefiros are like a source from which the revealed Sefiros are drawn
[in the manner of the two aspects of "as water reflects a face back to a face" in water in its simple sense,
that the image of the face looking into them appears in the water,
an ascent from below to above,
and that the image appearing in the water is afterwards seen by the man looking,
a drawing down from above to below].

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the verse implies that the concept of "water reflecting a face" is simpler than "the heart of man to man," given that the disparity between the simple Ein Sof and the form of Sefiros is far greater than that between lower and upper man.
section.t: And it must be understood,
that from that which it is said "as water reflects a face back to a face, so the heart of man to man," it implies,
that the matter of "water reflects a face back to a face" is simpler than the matter of "the heart of man to man,"
and at first glance,
behold, the incomparability of form
("face")
relative to simplicity
("water")
is far greater than the incomparability of the form of the lower man relative to the form of the upper Man
[as per the well-known statement,
"More than the incomparability of Asiyah relative to Atzilus is the incomparability of Atzilus relative to Ein Sof"],
and accordingly,
that through the raising of feminine waters a form of Sefiros is made in Ein Sof is seemingly a far greater novelty than that the form of the lower man is made in the upper Man,
and from that which it is said "as water reflects a face back to a face, so the heart of man to man," it implies,
that the matter of "water reflects a face back to a face" is simpler.
